items.title: Gold surges as oil slump eases inflation fears

featured_image.name: Gold jumps 2% as oil slump eases inflation fears amid Trump Iran talks

items.description:
Gold prices climbed sharply on Wednesday as a steep decline in oil prices eased inflation concerns and tempered expectations for interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, even as mixed signals over a potential U.S.-Iran ceasefire kept markets on edge.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to around $4,551 per ounce, while gold futures for April delivery jumped more than 3%, according to CNBC. The rally came as oil prices sank more than 5% on optimism that Washington was pursuing a diplomatic path to pause the conflict, with Brent crude falling to roughly $99 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropping to around $88.[1][2]

items.title: AI detects landslide risks years in advance using satellite radar data

featured_image.name: AI Predicts Landslides with Enhanced Precision

items.description:
Around the village of Kimtang in central Nepal, cracks run through concrete steps and trees grow at odd angles — signs that the ground is shifting beneath residents' feet. Scientists at the University of Melbourne have used artificial intelligence to analyze satellite radar data and confirm what villagers long suspected: their homes sit atop an unstable slope at high risk of a devastating landslide. The AI marked the danger zone in bright red on a color map, a warning that could prove lifesaving.[1][2]

The Nepal project is part of a growing wave of research applying AI to one of the world's most destructive and difficult-to-predict natural hazards. In the first two months of 2026 alone, 91 fatal landslides killed more than 800 people worldwide, according to data tracked by Eos. Researchers across multiple continents are now racing to deploy machine learning systems that can detect the subtle ground movements that precede catastrophic slope failures.[3]

items.title: Iran mocks US ceasefire plan, says Americans 'negotiating with yourselves'

featured_image.name: Americans were negotiating with themselves': Iran mocks US ...

items.description:
President Trump's assertion that the United States is engaged in productive negotiations with Iran to end the month-old war has been met with open derision from Tehran, where an Iranian military spokesperson on Wednesday said the Americans "are negotiating with yourselves."[1]

Lt. Col. Ebrahim Zolfaghari, speaking in a prerecorded video on Iranian state television, dismissed Trump's diplomatic overtures. "Don't dress up your defeat as an agreement. Your era of empty promises has come to an end," he said, according to the Associated Press. His remarks came shortly after the Trump administration delivered a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran through Pakistani intermediaries.[2][3][1]

items.title: NASA confirms Artemis II is go for April 1 moon launch

featured_image.name: When is Nasa's Moon mission launch and what will Artemis do? - BBC

items.description:
Four astronauts are one week away from becoming the first humans to travel to the moon in more than half a century. NASA is targeting April 1 for the launch of Artemis 2, a 10-day test flight that will send a crew around the far side of the moon and back aboard the Orion spacecraft atop the Space Launch System rocket.[1][2]

The crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch from NASA, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — entered quarantine in Houston on March 18 and will fly to Kennedy Space Center roughly five days before launch. The mission will make Glover the first person of color, Koch the first woman, and Hansen the first non-American to travel to the moon.[3][4][2]

items.title: Astronomers spot two planets forming around a young star like our sun

featured_image.name: Astronomers have spotted two giant gas plants forming around ...

items.description: An international team of astronomers has confirmed the discovery of a second planet forming in the dust disk surrounding the young star WISPIT 2, making it only the second known system where two planets have been directly observed taking shape around their host star. The findings, published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, offer what researchers describe as the closest analog yet to our own solar system in its infancy.[1][2]

items.title: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds

featured_image.name: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health ...

items.description:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ruled on Tuesday to place former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds, reversing months of denied requests from the right-wing leader's legal team, according to Reuters.[1]

Bolsonaro, 71, has been serving a 27-year prison sentence since November for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The house arrest will last for an initial 90-day period, after which Moraes said conditions will be reassessed. "The presence of the requirements necessary for maintaining humanitarian house arrest will be reassessed, including a medical examination if needed," the justice wrote in the decision.[1]

items.title: Israeli airstrike hits Christian town north of Beirut for first time

featured_image.name: Airstrike hits Lebanese Christian town north of Beirut ...

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck the Christian town of Sahel Alma north of Beirut on Tuesday, marking the first time the area had been targeted in the expanding war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to Lebanese state media and Reuters. There were no immediate reports of casualties, but witnesses told Reuters they heard several blasts and saw white smoke rising from the town.[1][2][3]

The strike represents a widening of Israel's air campaign into areas previously untouched by the conflict, which has killed more than 1,000 people in Lebanon and displaced over one million since fighting escalated on March 2.[4][5]
